sol.problem: TDL-9 says exhaustion "stops the generation ... no further source instruction executes", but §18.4 requires for ctrl/adj that "every register allocated during the generation is freed during it", otherwise T-LEAK. Witness: an action body executes `%h = call ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 0, i64 1); call void @__bennett_gate(i32 1, ptr %h, i64 0); call void @__bennett_gate(i32 1, ptr %h, i64 0); call void @__bennett_qfree(ptr %h); ret void`. With one G step it records qalloc, exhausts before the first gate, and never reaches qfree. Literal leak checking traps with code 4 during generation, even when the outer control is 0; TDL-9 instead promises code 1 under that control. Suppressing the trap alone leaves an unmatched allocation. This is an interaction introduced by the D02-08 fix, not a demand for a cleanup proof.
sol.fix: State in TDL-9 and §18.4: "Generation exhaustion is an invocation failure, not a source leak. Compiler finalization runs after exhaustion without consuming the exhausted generation budget. By default, abort before applying recorded events: discard the invocation's speculative views and recorders, cancel its invocation-owned provisional allocations, preserve foreign handles, and emit only the appropriate fault event under its invocation/path controls. Failed compute generation does not execute use; failure of either part cancels the still-unapplied composite invocation. Normal T-LEAK checking applies to a successfully completed source generation." Alternatively preserve the prefix with an explicit reversible cleanup of every local allocation/workspace; I would cancel the recorder because §18.4 records before application. Add the witness: no local h remains live, foreign registers are unchanged, control=0 gives Φ=0, control=1 gives Φ=1, and neither branch traps T-LEAK/T-CLEAN.

sol.section: §8.5 empty-R optimization and snapshot reuse; §16.2 prologue
sol.problem: §8.5 promises a "private copy of the caller's whole classical memory" and says replay makes heap_used/atop equal caller entry values, but omits transfer when the load read-set R is empty. Allocation state affects results without loading caller bytes. Use §16.9's normative malloc body, just __bennett_nz_alloc: a CC caller has already allocated 16 bytes at heap_base=4096, then invokes an oracle containing malloc(16), ptrtoint and return, with no alloca or other memory load. R is empty and no stack-use addition applies. The prescribed fresh wrapper returns 4096; private caller-state execution returns 4112. Both succeed with sufficient budget. Independently checked/hashed ISA probes through the supplied interpreter via stdin confirmed payloads 4096 versus 4112, code 0. Snapshot reuse also invalidates only on "store to an object of R"; allocation/free changes k, bump or live bits without such a store.
sol.fix: State in §8.5: "Entry-state dependencies include allocation history/liveness metadata whenever the closure may allocate, free, validate caller storage or observe an allocation-derived address. Replay k, sizes and live bits in these cases even when the byte read-set is empty; include bytes only as required by byte dependencies. Omit replay only when both byte and allocator-state dependencies are absent. Invalidate cached snapshots on relevant alloc/free and shadow-stack push/pop/restore operations as well as stores." Apply this decision in §16.2 before private allocations. The witness returns 4112, code 0, preserving caller state; after another caller allocation of 16 bytes, the next invocation returns 4128. Replaying full allocation history for allocation-sensitive closures is the sound default; a smaller proven dependency is optional.

sol.problem: §12.6 includes "casts" among elementwise instructions, but LLVM bitcast can change lane count/width or cross scalar/vector boundaries. No other N21 row handles that case. Little-endian witness: `%v = load <2 x i32>, ptr %p, align 1; %b = bitcast <2 x i32> %v to <4 x i16>; %r = extractelement <4 x i16> %b, i32 1; ret i16 %r`, with bytes 44 33 22 11 88 77 66 55. Correct result is 0x1122 (4386). An elementwise i32-to-i16 bitcast is illegal and cannot produce four lanes; retaining the vector violates V13/§16.1. LLVM 18 and 23 verify and fold the equivalent constant-pattern probe to `ret i16 4386`. The missing expansion also leaves canonical row counts, hence F_B, undefined for an accepted construct.
sol.fix: Add to §12.6: "Bitcast is elementwise only when source and destination lane geometries agree. Otherwise form the source packed bit string in datalayout order and resegment it into destination lanes or a scalar. On supported little-endian targets, lane 0 occupies the low bits. The default expansion zero-extends source carriers to total width, shifts by cumulative widths and ORs in increasing source-lane order; extracts destination lanes by logical right shift and truncation in increasing destination-lane order, omitting identity casts and zero shifts. N22 legalises total widths above 128. Legalization drops no source memory access." Add scalar↔vector and lane-changing pairs. For the witness retain both i32 loads at offsets 0/4 and return trunc.i16(lshr.i32(first_load,16))=4386, code 0. Rejecting the cast would narrow scope.

sol.section: §12.6 N21 blanket llvm.vp.* rule; Appendix C
sol.problem: The blanket VP rule defines active as k<evl and mask[k], with inactive lanes yielding 0 except masked-load passthrough. That is false for VP selection: false-condition lanes have defined values. Witness: `%v = call <2 x i32> @llvm.vp.merge.v2i32(<2 x i1> <i1 true,i1 false>, <2 x i32> <i32 5,i32 6>, <2 x i32> <i32 7,i32 9>, i32 2); %r = extractelement <2 x i32> %v, i32 1`. The blanket rule gives 0; LLVM gives 9. LLVM 18/23 verify the module; LLVM 23 native lowering independently emits `movl $9, %eax; retq`. Installed LLVM 23 VPIntrinsics.def explicitly says vp.select/vp.merge do not report their condition as a predication mask because false lanes have defined results. Appendix C promises both names.
sol.fix: State in §12.6: "The generic inactive-zero rule applies only where the intrinsic's LangRef result is poison. For vp.select/vp.merge the condition is a selector, not an inactivity mask: within explicit vector length lower each lane to select(condition[k], on_true[k], on_false[k]). Preserve each intrinsic's specified behavior outside that length and replace only poison by N7 zero; vp.merge preserves its on_false value outside the selected active prefix as well." Give these rules precedence over the generic bullet. Add the witness as a normalisation/native pair returning 9, plus an analogous vp.select false-condition witness. Also state: "VP reductions fold the start value with active lanes only, in increasing lane order; inactive lanes contribute no zero unless zero is that reduction's identity." This prevents the blanket rule from zeroing masked products/AND reductions.

codex.problem: §17.1 requires every access to lie wholly in one live allocation. TDL-4 puts distinct globals and coherent heap objects into one arena, while §16.3 removes their individual global entries and §16.4 checks only the ISA allocation containing the address. ISA §7.2 gives the whole coh interface region one pinned live entry. Thus logical object bounds and liveness disappear. Use the arena-o1 layout with two distinct one-byte globals at offsets 0 and 1, containing 01 and 02. A slice performing load i16 at offset 0 must fault 7: neither global contains both bytes. The specified boundscheck/load rows instead succeed with 513. I reproduced this by adapting arena-o1 in an anonymous memory file, updating its hashes, and running the supplied interpreter: check accepted; run-oracle with coh=0102, arg=0 and budget=100,0,32,1 returned code=0, payload=513, steps=7. Arena padding and freed coherent allocations have the same missing validation. This is a dialect-to-ISA mapping defect, not an ISA gap.
codex.fix: In TDL-4 and §16.4 state: "The arena interface range is storage, not a logical allocation. Maintain the base, size and live state of each arena object. Before every program-memory access of n bytes at p, require that the entire nonwrapping range [p,p+n) lies in one live logical allocation; otherwise produce fault 7 before the access. The pinned coh entry does not satisfy this logical check." Use an ordinary materialised runtime helper over this metadata as the default, with its rows charged in the reference object; apply the same validation to event-producing stores and gate their mutation on success. Include coherent allocator allocation/free updates and metadata transfer in the contract. Retain one physical coh region so superposed addressing remains available. Correct witness: the spanning i16 load gives payload=0/code=7, whereas either separate i8 load succeeds with 1 or 2.

codex.problem: §8.5 promises a private copy of the caller's whole memory and allocator state, but R is still selected from objects the closure may load; "if R is empty, no transfer runs". Allocation primitives read hidden allocator state without an LLVM load. Consider a caller that has allocated 16 bytes at heap_base=4096 and then invokes a materialised oracle consisting only of p=__bennett_nz_alloc(1); return ptrtoint(p). It has no load, global or shadow-stack use, so R is empty and its reference object starts with heap_used=0. It returns 4096; the promised call-entry-state execution returns 4112. With heap budget 16, the inherited-state execution must instead fault 2, while the fresh-heap map succeeds. The stack-adoption fix does not cover this allocation-only closure. Reusing a snapshot solely because no store to R occurred can also miss intervening alloc/free operations.
codex.fix: In §8.5 state: "Allocation, deallocation and allocation-validity checks read allocator metadata even when the closure contains no LLVM load. Treat that metadata as an entry-state dependency. Replay the caller's allocation history and live bits whenever those operations can execute, independently of the byte read set; an empty byte read set does not permit resetting allocator state. Snapshot reuse requires unchanged dependent allocation metadata as well as unchanged dependent bytes." Default to replaying the complete allocation table for any closure with such a dependency; bytes may still be omitted when unread. Add the allocation-only witness: after the caller's 16-byte allocation, sufficient-budget payload=4112/code=0, and heap budget 16 gives payload=0/code=2. Neither oracle invocation changes the caller's allocation state.

codex.problem: The compute-specific recorder fix leaves ordinary nested generations inconsistent. TDL-2 checks enclosing recorders for Co writes, but a Cl byte is still "the shadow updated by the recorder's own classical events". Parent events have not been applied while the parent recorder is active (§18.2). Witness: t starts Cl(0); outer f stores 9 to t and calls ctrl(c2,g), where g flips target z iff t==9; invoke f under c1, with both controls equal to 1 and z=0. The child has no own write to t, K(t) is still Cl, and the parent's unpredicated xmask is not a Co write. The literal child view reads shadow 0, so it omits the flip. The sequential branch semantics promised by TDL-2/§18.4 reads the parent's 9 and flips z. The new retained-recorder sentence applies to compute, not this nested ctrl.
codex.fix: Replace the Cl-view sentence in TDL-2 with: "A child generation inherits the invoking generation's current speculative view. A Cl byte is obtained by applying the visible enclosing recorders' classical updates in execution order, then the child's own updates, to the invocation-entry shadow. The enclosing invocation control is not added to that inherited view until event composition. Co writes remain Co, and sibling branch recorders remain isolated until the join." Apply this to nested ctrl, adj and compute consistently with branch-local views. Add the witness with expected events xmask t+0 0x09 ctrl c1; x z ctrl c1 c2. For c1=c2=1 the final t is 9 and z is 1; for c1=0 both remain zero.

codex.section: §12.2 n-defined-zero; §12.4 V4 and validator-v4-clean; §12.8 N27; Appendix C
codex.problem: The new examples contradict the existing materialisation boundary. N27 explicitly replaces ctlz and cttz with __bennett_rt_<name>_i<W> calls; Appendix C assigns them to N27; V4 rejects any intrinsic N27 removes. Nevertheless n-defined-zero's full normalise-out retains both LLVM intrinsics, and validator-v4-clean says "ctlz with false is retained" and requires accept for a residual llvm.ctlz.i8 call. A validator following V4 rejects that exact positive example; one following the example accepts it. §16.4 also has no retained ctlz row. Correctly setting the N12 poison flag is an intermediate step, not the specified full N27 output.
codex.fix: Keep N27 and add to §12.2/§12.4: "N12 totalises the flag before N27; it does not exempt abs, ctlz or cttz from their later expansion. Full materialised output contains no calls to these LLVM intrinsics, including false-flag calls." Change n-defined-zero's output calls to %a = call i8 @__bennett_rt_ctlz_i8(i8 %x, i1 false) and %b = call i8 @__bennett_rt_cttz_i8(i8 %x, i1 false), with matching runtime declarations/definitions; the add and returns remain unchanged. Give validator-v4-clean the materialised helper form, and make residual ctlz(false) a negative V4 witness alongside ctlz(true). Expected f(0)=16 and f(1)=7 remain unchanged. Alternatively retaining these intrinsics requires changing N27, V4, Appendix C and adding a canonical §16 row; I would keep the existing runtime-expansion design.

muse.problem: Per-slice fault registers have no defined release, and the literal text traps its own examples. TDL-8: 'f_k holds the slice's code and is retained (TDL-7)' and firstfault XORs the first nonzero code into Phi, but no rule ever frees f_k (or compute's retained copies g_k), and on a faulting branch f_k holds a nonzero code entangled with the inputs, so qreg.free would violate ISA §3.3 cleanliness (dialect T-CLEAN). §18.4's leak rule says for ctrl/adj 'every register allocated during the generation is freed during it'; the tdl-b event list frees m1 and f1b but never f1 or Phi1. Reading A (leak rule covers plugin registers): every slice-containing invocation traps T-LEAK, contradicting tdl-b's state vectors. Reading B (plugin frees f_k after the combine): T-CLEAN trap exactly on faulting branches. Reading C (retain unmeasured past return): no trap. Reading D (measure plugin Phi/f_k at 'the CC epilogue', a point the text never defines - invocation end, device-entry return, or program end): frees via measurement at an unspecified time. Trap versus no trap on the same program is an observable divergence.
muse.fix: In §10 TDL-8 and §18.4 state: 'The registers f_k, compute's copies g_k and a plugin-allocated Phi are declared fault outputs of the invocation owned by the CC tier. They are exempt from the §18.4 leak rule, are neither measured nor freed at invocation return or device-entry return, and are released only at program end: each is measured for the run's fault statistics and freed after outcome-conditioned X corrections. No f_k is freed at the firstfault combine; adjoint(E_f) reuses the same f_k wires (as f9 in tdl-d). The CC epilogue of TDL-8 is this program-end release.' Add a state= witness: a slice that faults with code 1 on one superposed branch, budget fault field null; after the invocation: no T-LEAK/T-CLEAN, Phi=1 on that branch, data state otherwise as tdl-b; at program end the statistics record code 1 with the branch probability. The alternative (accumulate into Phi at slice time and clean each f_k with its own uncomputing call into the same register, retaining only Phi) is also acceptable if spelled out; I would take the retained-declared-outputs rule as the smaller change.

muse.problem: Three rules contradict each other for a loop whose trip count is Co. TDL-10 unrolls it with flags c_i (c_{i+1} = c_i and condition_i via ccx into fresh wires) and says 'the flags are history (TDL-7)'. The rewritten TDL-7 has no history category: 'Non-fault workspace ... MUST be cleaned by the adjoint of its exact computing sequence before the invocation returns; it is never implicitly made an output or measured.' But the flags cannot in general be cleaned at loop exit: uncomputing c_{i+1} needs condition_i recomputed from iteration-i state, which later iterations have overwritten (e.g. for (i < @n) @cnt += 1, or a condition reading a byte the body flips). And §18.2's adjoint (reverse the list, ccx self-adjoint) uses the flag wires before anything computes them in a standalone adj(body), unlike ISA §5.3's special qloop-while adjoint ('flags computed forward; adj A for i=n..1 under c_i; flags uncomputed'). Implementer readings diverge observably: retain flags (leak trap per BD3-1 reading A), free them dirty (T-CLEAN), measure them (the channel D02-05 removed), or reject Co loops (narrows NS §4.2 coherent internal control). No example exercises a Co-trip-count loop in an action body.
muse.fix: Replace 'the flags are history (TDL-7)' in TDL-10 with: 'The flags c_i and the per-iteration condition wires are retained declared control outputs of the invocation, with the fault-register lifecycle of TDL-8 (leak-exempt, unmeasured until program end). The adjoint of an unrolled Co loop is a special case in §18.2, not plain ccx reversal: conditions and flags are computed forward from the preserved inputs, body adjoints run for i = N..1 under c_i, then flags and conditions are uncomputed in reverse. Inside compute(f, ...) adjoint(E_f) reuses and cleans the same flag wires.' Add a tdl=/state= witness: body B = 'for (i = 0; i < @n; i++) @cnt = add @cnt, 1' with @n in (|0>+|2>)/sqrt(2), @cnt = 0, steps budget 4: after adj(B) then compute(B, use) the state during use is (|n=0,cnt=0> + |n=2,cnt=2>)/sqrt(2) up to retained flags, after compute @cnt = 0 on both branches with flags clean, no trap; standalone adj(B) from |n=2,cnt=2> gives cnt=0. The alternative (clean flags at loop exit, restricting Co loops to conditions computed from wires the body does not modify, ISA qloop-style, with a named rejection otherwise) narrows NS §4.2 and should not be taken.

muse.problem: D02-06's fix is undone on the adjoint paths. §7.5(a) now requires retaining the qcopy outcome record to a measurement boundary ('an open window alone never justifies quncopy'), but §18.2 states without exception 'qcopy and quncopy are mutual adjoints', and §7.7's non-normative note still describes the old rule ('w released by the region's uncomputation'). For adj(f) where f defers a measurement, gen(f) records E = [qcopy a.0 -> w, cx w t.0, ...] and the marker applies adjoint(E) = [..., cx w t.0, quncopy a.0 w]: w is used before any event allocates or copies into it, and the closing quncopy XORs a into a fresh |0> wire, which is then not clean (T-CLEAN) - and where it does not trap it erases exactly the measurement channel §7.5(a) forbids erasing. The same erasure occurs inside compute(f, use) when adjoint(E_f) quncopies f's record before any boundary. Two readings of adj on |+> with an unused deferred measure then H then measure: keep-record gives P(0)=P(1)=1/2 (deferred-channel witness), adjoint-table gives a trap or P(0)=1.
muse.fix: In §7.5(a) and §18.2 state: 'A deferred-measurement qcopy is never adjointed to quncopy. In a standalone adj(f), each qcopy of E is emitted again as a qcopy onto a fresh retained record wire, placed before (in application order) every adjointed event predicated on it, and measured under the same boundary rule; all other events are adjointed as §18.2 states. Inside compute(f, use), records created in E_f are retained through E_u and adjoint(E_f) (which reuses the same record wires and does not quncopy them) and are measured at the first boundary after compute returns.' Correct the §7.7 note to the same rule. Add state=deferred-channel-adj: defer flag set, body measures q unused, invoked by adj, q = |+>, then H(q), measure(q) -> P(0)=1/2, P(1)=1/2, no T-CLEAN. The alternative (reject deferring candidates for adj as BD-E-REGION-MEASURE) narrows the deferral capability and I would not take it.

muse.problem: BLK-5 has no classification rule, so the module verdict (a compile-time observable: exit 0 versus distinct status 3, §1.6) is ambiguous for every R program. §11.5: typed R faults have 'verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA7 at affected points'; §17.6 inserts a step counter in every R variant whose exhaustion is __bennett_nz_fault(1), and materialisation inserts F(C) points (trapped calls, N11, runtimes fault sites such as ss_push overflow) in ordinary R closures, so under §1.6 ('blocked: at least one program point needs a capability ISA 0.8 cannot express') essentially every module with R-tier code is blocked. Yet region-reversible-marker, region-reversible-qalloc-static, effect-console-r, sjlj-two-frames, fiber-pingpong, exit-status and platform-uart-write all carry verdict=accept, while the two materialised-IR examples r-budget-prefix and r-fault-code carry blocked:BD-B-ISA7. One plugin returns accept (and then must either report a generic trap code on exhaustion, violating §17.5/§18.7, or silently claim the typed contract §17.6 says is 'not claimed implemented'); another returns blocked for the same module. §25.1's blocker trap ('hostcall bennett.fault ... then trap (§11.5)') is also stated in its CC form only; R cannot hostcall, so the R blocker-trap form is undefined.
muse.fix: State one rule in §11.5 and §25.1; I would take: 'On ISA 0.8 a module whose device program contains an R-tier variant reached as an R entry (a reversible region candidate, or the §19.2 whole-program R mode) has verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA7. The blocker trap in R is the ISA generic trap with no hostcall, reached only on executions that would report a typed fault (budget exhaustion, F(C), nz_fault(C)); all other executions are unaffected. A reversible call treated as a direct call under §7.4 is not an R entry and does not by itself block the module.' Retag region-reversible-marker, region-reversible-qalloc-static, effect-console-r, sjlj-two-frames, fiber-pingpong, exit-status and platform-uart-write to verdict=blocked:BD-B-ISA7 with their blocker= lines; their cc-run/state expectations are unchanged. The viable alternative (blocked only when the materialised R closure contains an explicit nz_fault/F(C) point, budget counters excluded by a stated generic-trap semantics for exhaustion on ISA 0.8) reintroduces D02-21's divergent fault codes and depends on run-time budget values, so I would not take it.

muse.problem: The reference instance bound is unsound under longjmp re-entry, because setjmp's second return is invisible to the CFG/call-graph conditions. Rule 1 deems a site self-disjoint (N(s)=1) when every CFG path from s to a ret, to s again, or to 'a call whose callee may reach F through the call graph' passes a qfree of exactly {s}; rule 2 counts executions from loop trip counts and call sites. Witness (CC-tier F, handle stored in two non-escaping allocas so the site needs the static file): 'while (1) { r = setjmp(b); h = qalloc(0,1); store h into slot[r]; if (r) break; g(); break; } free both slots' where g longjmps to b on its first call. Execution: setjmp returns 0, qalloc #1 -> slot[0], g longjmps, setjmp returns 1 at the same site, qalloc #2 executes with #1 still live. In the source CFG there is no path from s back to s avoiding qfree, and g does not reach F in the §4.1 call graph (it calls the runtimes longjmp), so the text gives N(s)=1: the second qalloc has no free instance, and the plugin must trap, reuse the live register (aliasing two distinct handles), or invent behaviour - all different from the reference semantics (two registers, both freed, no trap). E(s) in rule 2 undercounts the same way, and §7.5(b) R-hoisting inherits both by reference.
muse.fix: Add to §6.5 before rules 1-2: 'For rules 1 and 2 the CFG of F is taken after adding, for every setjmp site in F (N29, §14.5), an edge from every call instruction in F to that setjmp's continuation, and the setjmp call itself counts as a call that may reach F. A site reachable from such a continuation is self-disjoint only if every added-edge path also passes the qfree; E(s) counts executions over the augmented CFG.' A simpler sufficient default ('if F contains a setjmp site whose continuation can reach s, s is not self-disjoint and E(s) = infinity') is also acceptable; I would take the added-edge version since it keeps bounded cases accepted. Add a checked example of the witness above: with the added-edge rule N(s)=2, verdict accept, both handles gate distinct registers and both qfree clean (under the simple default: blocked:BD-B-ISA4 - state which).

muse.problem: Classical accesses to a Co object outside any generation are defined only for reads. TDL-11 bullet 2 compiles 'code outside every region that may read a may-Co object' in Cl/Co variants with the Co variant trapping T-TAINT-HOST; TDL-4 rewrites CC loads/stores to address+delta_sh 'when the object's state is Cl or M' and says 'when the state is Co, TDL-11 applies'; TDL-2 gives Co->Cl transitions only by full observe 'also by its release (free, end of lifetime)'. Witness 1: in @tdl_a insert 'store i8 0, ptr @cnt' between ctrl(@bump) (which leaves @cnt Co in (|0>+|5>)/sqrt(2)) and observe. Reading A (store rewritten to shadow): the store is silently lost because the arena is authoritative, observe still returns 0/5 - a classical write with no effect. Reading B (T-TAINT-HOST by analogy with reads): fault 4. Reading C (dematerialise-then-store): impossible for Co without measurement. Witness 2: free of a Co heap object (inside or outside a generation) followed by coherent-allocator reuse of its cells: TDL-2's unconditional 'Co -> Cl by release' restores the Cl invariant 'arena cells are |0>' only on paper, so the next object's materialisation XORs its shadow into superposed garbage and slices read the garbage; TDL-12's 'release requires clean/restored state' names no trap or code when it is not clean.
muse.fix: Extend TDL-11 bullet 2 to all CC accesses and fix TDL-2: 'Code outside every generation that may load from, store to, free or otherwise release an object traps T-TAINT-HOST (code 4) on executions where that object's dynamic state is Co; a CC store to such an object is legal only after __bennett_observe of every byte it writes. Release of an object whose state is Co (free, end of lifetime, inside or outside a generation) traps T-TAINT-HOST unless its arena cells are first restored to the basis state equal to its shadow by the invocation's own events (e.g. adjoint(E_f)), in which case it is dematerialised and released as Cl. Delete TDL-2's unconditional Co->Cl by release.' Add witnesses: (1) the @tdl_a store variant -> T-TAINT-HOST code 4, and the observe-first variant -> store wins, subsequent load returns 0 on both branches; (2) alloc/write-Co/free/realloc inside one adj -> trap at free, no garbage read.
